lines.japanese: ちょっと恥ずかしいけど、まずは初めて彼女と目が合った日のことを君に話してしまおう。
lines.english: It's a little embarrassing, but I suppose I should start by telling you about the first time our eyes met.

lines.japanese: それはまだ入学式からひと月も経っていない、ある四月の晴れた午後。
lines.english: It was a clear April afternoon, less than a month after the entrance ceremony.

lines.japanese: 異種族の襲撃を退けてグレタガルドから帰ってくると、美空学園ではすでに昼休みが始まっていた。
lines.english: I'd just returned from Gretagard after repelling an attack by another race. Here at Misora Academy, lunch break had already begun.

lines.japanese: やけに白さの目立つ新設校舎の教室。窓の外には隣りの高層ビル、そして大都会・柳木原のほの白い空。
lines.english: A classroom in the new building, still glaringly white. Through the windows: the high-rise next door, and beyond it the pale sky over the great city of Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 机同士をくっつけた食卓がまわりに点在する中、僕の席は島嶼部に浮かんだちっぽけな孤島みたいにはぐれ者だった。
lines.english: Clusters of desks had been pushed together into lunch tables all around me. My seat stood apart, a tiny island set adrift from the archipelago.

lines.japanese: 入学してひと月、まだ名前も覚えきっていないクラスメイトの喧騒は、羨ましいぐらいに平和そのものだった。
lines.english: A month into school, I still hadn’t learned all my classmates’ names. Their noisy chatter was peace itself—enviably so.

lines.japanese: さっきまで血しぶき舞う戦場で命の削り合いをしていたのが嘘みたいな、楽園ののどかな昼下がり。
lines.english: A sleepy afternoon in paradise. You would never have guessed that moments before, I had been fighting for my life on a battlefield spattered with blood.

lines.japanese: たくさんの笑い声が折りかさなった教室で、人知れず僕だけが肩で息をしていた。
lines.english: Laughter filled the classroom, voice upon voice. In the middle of it all, I alone sat gasping for breath, unnoticed.

lines.japanese: 誰の目にも映ってはいない小さな光の粒が、僕の体からひっそりキャンプファイヤーの火の粉みたいに立ちのぼって消えてゆく。
lines.english: Specks of light no one else could see rose silently from my body like sparks from a campfire, then winked out.

lines.japanese: だけどまだ全身の筋肉は強張っていて、心臓の拍動が痛いぐらいに速かった。
lines.english: Every muscle in my body was still clenched. My heart beat fast enough to hurt.

lines.japanese: 冷めた海苔や揚げ物の香る立方体の中、僕は呆けたように、机の上へ投げだされていた自分の手のひらに視線を落とした。
lines.english: In that box of a room, smelling of cold seaweed and fried food, I stared numbly at the hand lying open on my desk.

lines.japanese: かすかに長剣の重みが残ったそれは細かく震えていた。
lines.english: It still held the ghost of a longsword's weight, and trembled faintly beneath it.

lines.japanese: 黒ずんだ肉に鋼を埋めこみ、その骨を力まかせに砕きわった感触──
lines.english: The feel of steel sinking into blackened flesh, of bone breaking under the force of the blow—

lines.japanese: ──は、しかし、濡れた手が乾いていくようにじわじわと消えうせてゆく。
lines.english: —was slowly fading, the way wet hands dry.

lines.japanese: ひと呼吸ごとに体は落ち着きを取りもどす。緊張していた筋肉がほぐれ血管が広がってゆく様を、まざまざと体感しているようだった。
lines.english: Each breath brought my body closer to calm. I could almost feel the tight muscles slacken and the blood vessels open.

lines.japanese: しわがれた断末魔のうめきがまだ鼓膜にこびりついてる気もするけれど、それはもはや幻聴だ。
lines.english: A hoarse death groan still seemed to cling to my eardrums, but now it was only a phantom echo.

lines.japanese: 向こうでの記憶なんて、こっちに戻ってきてたかだか数瞬で消える。明け方に見た悪夢と同じで、あとに残るのは漠然とした高揚感の輪郭だけ。
lines.english: Memories of that world disappeared within moments of my return to this one. Like a nightmare at dawn, they left behind nothing but the blurred outline of exhilaration.

lines.japanese: 戦いの余韻に浸る間もなく、その恐怖や興奮は、中空におどる金色の粒子とともにはかなく霧散する。
lines.english: Before I could savor the afterglow of battle, the fear and excitement dissolved with the golden particles dancing in the air.

lines.japanese: こうなってしまえば僕なんて、もはや敵を断つ剣も身を守る武具もない、ただの美空学園の新入生（当時）だ。
lines.english: And then I was nobody again: merely an empty-handed greenhorn at Misora Academy—a freshman, back then—with no sword to strike down an enemy and no armor to save my skin.

lines.japanese: ここでは、僕が人々から賞賛と尊敬を勝ちうることもない。この厳然たる事実は、平和な楽園へ戻ってきた僕をいつも少しばかり虚しい気持ちにさせる。
lines.english: No one here would praise or revere me. Whenever I came home to this peaceful paradise, that stark fact left me a little hollow.

lines.japanese: もし僕がこの世界でも勇者であったなら……。
lines.english: If only I could be a hero in this world too…

lines.japanese: 流行りのコメディアンの口真似をしている級友たちから取りのこされて、僕はひとり非生産的な夢想にふける。
lines.english: My classmates did impressions of whatever comedians were popular that week while I, left out as usual, indulged in a thoroughly useless daydream.

lines.japanese: もしやつらが──グレタガルドに跋扈する、血の気の多い亜人種や飢えた幻想生物が──こののどかな楽園に流れこんでその歯牙を剥いたなら。
lines.english: What if they came here? What if the bloodthirsty demihumans and starving beasts that roamed Gretagard poured into this quiet paradise and bared their fangs?

lines.japanese: きっと同級生も学園長も総理大臣も、誰もがみな僕を畏怖し恭順することになるだろう。
lines.english: My classmates, the headmaster, the prime minister—every one of them would tremble before me and bend the knee.

lines.japanese: ……なんて、くだらない。
lines.english: …How stupid.

lines.japanese: のどかな楽園に戻ってきた徒手空拳の青二才には、そんな風に溜息を漏らすことと、せいぜいが声にも出さず祈ることしか出来ない。
lines.english: An empty-handed greenhorn, newly returned to his peaceful paradise, could do little more than sigh at himself and pray without even saying the words aloud.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: 「おい、羽田ァ！」
lines.english: “Hey! Hanedaaa!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: とつぜん背中にもみじ型の判を捺され、僕の体は物音を聞きつけた小動物みたいにびくりと跳ねた。
lines.english: A maple-leaf handprint was suddenly stamped between my shoulder blades. I jumped like a small animal at the snap of a twig.

lines.japanese: 後ろに立っていたのは、肩までの長髪が奔放な性格によく似合う、森里和馬という名の同級生だった。
lines.english: Behind me stood my classmate Kazuma Morisato. His wild, shoulder-length hair suited his equally wild personality.

lines.japanese: グレタガルドが版図拡大を狙う異種族国家との戦渦に巻きこまれたせいで、僕は入学式前後あたりから向こうに≪召喚≫される機会が増えていた。
lines.english: Gretagard had been swept into a war with another race bent on expanding its borders, and ever since the days around the entrance ceremony I had been summoned there more and more often.

lines.japanese: だから僕はあちらで救国の士として英雄視されている分、こちらでは新入生たちによって構成されたどのグループにも入りそびれてしまった感があった。
lines.english: Over there, I was a hero who had helped save a nation. Here, I had somehow missed my chance to find a place in any of the groups formed by the new students.

lines.japanese: 森里君は、そんな僕に率先して話しかけてきてくれる数少ない──訂正、たったひとりの──クラスメイトだった。
lines.english: Morisato was one of the very few classmates who went out of his way to speak to me—correction, the only one.

lines.japanese: 「羽田、昼間っからなにトンでんだよ」
lines.english: “Haneda, what're you spacing out for in broad daylight?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ……おれ？」
lines.english: “Huh… Me?”

lines.japanese: 「そーだよ、さっきから呼んでんじゃん。おめ、どこの花畑行ってんだよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, you. I've been calling your name. What, were you off frolicking through a field of flowers?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あはは、ごめん……」
lines.english: “Oh. Ha-ha, sorry…”

lines.japanese: 森里君は横に立って腰を曲げ、座っている僕の肩に腕をまわした。
lines.english: Morisato bent over me and slipped an arm around my shoulders.

lines.japanese: ぐい、と引きよせるその一方的な力になぜか僕の体は萎縮する。
lines.english: He gave a tug. For some reason, that one-sided show of force made my body shrink into itself.

lines.japanese: 「あのさー羽田クン、悪りぃんだけどー」
lines.english: “Hey, Haneda. Sorry to do this to you, but…”

lines.japanese: 「うん……なに……」
lines.english: “Yes…? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 森里君はよく話しかけてくれるんだけど、それは頼みごとである場合が多かった。
lines.english: Morisato spoke to me often. Most of the time, it was because he wanted a favor.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっとさー、ブルガリ買ってきてくんねー？」
lines.english: “Could you go buy me some Bulgari?”

lines.japanese: 学食の自販機で売ってるブリック容器のヨーグルトドリンク。通称ブルガリ。
lines.english: A yogurt drink in a brick-shaped carton, sold in the cafeteria vending machines. Everyone called it Bulgari.

lines.japanese: 「うん。べつにいいけど」
lines.english: “Sure. I don't mind.”

lines.japanese: それでも僕を頼ってもらえるっていうのは嫌じゃなかった。むしろ嬉しかった。
lines.english: Still, I didn't mind having him rely on me. If anything, it made me happy.

lines.japanese: 「マジでぇー。いつも悪いねー。んじゃあ──」
lines.english: “For real? You're a lifesaver. Sorry I keep doing this to you. So—”

lines.japanese: じゃらじゃらっ。森里君は握りこんでいたこぶしを開いて、僕の胸ポケットに小銭を何枚か落としいれた。
lines.english: Clink, clatter. Morisato opened his fist and dropped a handful of coins into my breast pocket.

lines.japanese: 「──これで三つね。足んなかったら立てかえといて」
lines.english: “—three of 'em. If I'm short, spot me the rest.”

lines.japanese: 絡んだ腕がそのまま首に巻きついてくる。スリーパーホールド。彼はプロレスが好きらしく、僕はもっと複雑な関節技の練習相手を務めたこともあった。
lines.english: The arm across my shoulders curled around my neck. A sleeper hold. He apparently liked professional wrestling; I had even served as his practice dummy for more complicated joint locks.

lines.japanese: でもそれはどうやら僕だけの特権らしく、他のクラスメイトがその大任を果たしている場面はまだ見たことがなかった。
lines.english: That privilege seemed to belong to me alone. I had never seen him entrust any of our other classmates with so weighty a duty.

lines.japanese: こんなボーッとしたやつと仲良くしてくれる森里君が、僕はわりと好きだった。声の大きいところはちょっと苦手だけれど。
lines.english: I rather liked Morisato for being kind enough to befriend a space case like me. I could have done without the volume, though.

lines.japanese: 「あ、森里君。そういえばこの前の立て替え分、まだもらってないけど」
lines.english: “Oh, Morisato. That reminds me—you still haven't paid me back for last time.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、立て替えー？　んな、あったっけぇー？」
lines.english: “Paid you back? Did that happen?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ほら、おとといの、体育のあと……頼まれた分……」
lines.english: “You know. The day before yesterday, after gym… The things you asked me to get…”

lines.japanese: ぐい、ぐい──と交差した腕が喉首を絞めつけてくるので、ちょっと喋りにくかった。
lines.english: The arm locked across my throat squeezed tighter and tighter, making it difficult to speak.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そだっけー？　ごめんねー、いま細かいのコレだけだから、また今度でいいでしょー」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Did I? Sorry, this is all the change I've got, so next time's fine, yeah?”

lines.japanese: ぐい、ぐい、ぐい。
lines.english: Squeeze, squeeze, squeeze.

lines.japanese: 僕の横で森里君の長い髪が揺れる。ちらりと覗いた耳たぶに校則違反のピアスが光っていた。
lines.english: Morisato's long hair swayed beside me. Through it I glimpsed an earring, forbidden by school rules, gleaming in his exposed earlobe.

lines.japanese: 「うん……分かった……」
lines.english: “Okay… I understand…”

lines.japanese: 「さーんきゅー！　いッやあ、俺はいい友達持ったねマジで！」
lines.english: “Thaaanks! Man, I've got such a great friend. Seriously!”

lines.japanese: 森里君は僕の頭をくしゃくしゃと撫でまわした。トモダチという四文字に宿った言霊が、頭皮から塗りこめられていくみたいだった。
lines.english: Morisato scrubbed a hand through my hair. It was as if the magic lodged in the word friend were being rubbed into me through my scalp.

lines.japanese: だから僕は、首を絞められながら馬鹿みたいに微笑んでいた。
lines.english: So I smiled like an idiot while he strangled me.

lines.japanese: 「和馬ァー！　おいオメ、まだかよ！」
lines.english: “Kazumaaa! Hey, man, you done yet?”

lines.japanese: 「っせーな！　いま羽田クンとシンコー深めてんだよ！」
lines.english: “Shut up! I'm busy bonding with Haneda here!”

lines.japanese: 森里君は僕の頭の上で叫んだ。顎が当たってたから、頭蓋骨に声がじんじん響いた。
lines.english: Morisato shouted over my head. His chin was resting on me, so the sound rattled through my skull.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ羽田クン、昼休み終わんないうちにソッコー行ってきて」
lines.english: “Now get moving, Haneda. Quick, before lunch break's over.”

lines.japanese: 腕がほどけて、その手が僕の肩を力強く一回叩いた。
lines.english: His arm came loose, and the same hand gave my shoulder one hearty slap.

lines.japanese: 「うん、すぐ戻ってくる」
lines.english: “All right. I'll be right back.”

lines.japanese: 僕は乱れた襟を正しながら立ちあがった。すでに森里君は振りむきもせず、教室の後ろに固まっていた友人たちの方へ歩きはじめていた。
lines.english: I rose, straightening my rumpled collar. Morisato was already walking toward his friends at the back of the classroom without so much as a glance behind him.

lines.japanese: 教室のドアを開けながら、脈絡もなく僕は祈った。
lines.english: As I opened the classroom door, I prayed for no particular reason.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: 巨大なガラスの箱に、睡魔の化身みたいな春の陽射しが降りそそいでいた。
lines.english: Spring sunlight—the very incarnation of sleep—poured into the enormous glass box.

lines.japanese: オフィス街の景観が一望できる、もはやカフェテリアの呼び名こそ相応しい美空学園の学生食堂。
lines.english: Misora Academy’s dining hall overlooked the whole office district. With a view like that, it deserved to be called a café.

lines.japanese: 『開放的な空間でゆとりのある食事が気軽に楽しめます』
lines.english: “Enjoy a leisurely meal in a bright, open setting.”

lines.japanese: なんて、学校案内のパンフレットには書いてあったはずだけど、実際は上級生が「自主的に」管理する全席指定制だった。
lines.english: That was what the school brochure said, at least. In practice, every seat was assigned and “voluntarily” managed by the upperclassmen.

lines.japanese: 森里君から聞いたところによれば、学年・所属部・その他有力者とのコネクション等さまざまな条件をクリアした学生でないと、この賑やかな社交場には参加できないらしい。
lines.english: According to Morisato, admission to this lively social world depended on your year, your club, your connections to influential students, and any number of other qualifications.

lines.japanese: なんだか中世の貴族が集う紹介制のサロンみたいだ。
lines.english: It sounded like some invitation-only salon for medieval nobles.

lines.japanese: だったらここで昼の食事を取ることは三年間ないだろう、とあのころ新入生だった僕は、入り口脇の自販機前に立ちながらそう思ったものだ。
lines.english: Standing by the vending machines near the entrance, I remember deciding, as a brand-new student, that I would not eat lunch in there once during my three years at Misora.

lines.japanese: 足りない硬貨を自分の財布から補いつつ、僕は自動販売機の前に三回ひざまずいた。
lines.english: Making up the shortage from my own wallet, I knelt before the vending machines three times.

lines.japanese: そして三つの頼まれ物を抱えると、次に隅のパン売り場へ立ちよった。友達のジュースのついでに、自分の昼食も買っておこうと思ったからだ。
lines.english: With all three requested drinks in my arms, I stopped next at the bread counter in the corner. I thought I might as well buy my own lunch while I was there.

lines.japanese: 「すいません、うぐいすパンと、あと……」
lines.english: “Excuse me. A sweet green-pea bun, and…”

lines.japanese: しかし昼休みも半ばを過ぎて、ほとんど選択の余地は残っていなかった。
lines.english: But lunch break was more than half over, and there was almost nothing left to choose from.

lines.japanese: 「あと……野菜サンド……ください」
lines.english: “And… a vegetable sandwich, please.”

lines.japanese: 苦手なキュウリの青臭い風味を思うと、ちょっと気が滅入った。
lines.english: The thought of that raw green cucumber taste was enough to dampen my spirits.

lines.japanese: それから僕は、胸の前で組んだ腕の上に、ブルガリ三つとパン二つを載せて食堂を出た。
lines.english: I balanced the three Bulgaris and two kinds of bread across my folded arms and left the cafeteria.

lines.japanese: 売れない演歌歌手みたいな顔をしたパン売りのおばさんは、僕の溢れるような手荷物を見ても袋をくれなかった。
lines.english: The woman at the bread counter had the face of a ballad singer who’d never made it. Even after seeing my arms overflowing, she hadn’t given me a bag.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 泰然とした真っ白な廊下をすこし歩いたところで、ふと気付いた僕は来た道を引きかえした。
lines.english: A short way down the serenely white corridor, something occurred to me. I turned back.

lines.japanese: 自分の飲み物がない。
lines.english: I hadn't bought myself a drink.

lines.japanese: 僕はキュウリを円滑に呑みくだすための……たとえば烏龍茶が欲しかった。
lines.english: I needed something to help the cucumber go down. Oolong tea, for example.

lines.japanese: 戻ってきた自販機の前には、横幅のある男子生徒が立っていた。
lines.english: A broad male student stood at the vending machine when I returned.

lines.japanese: 僕と同じ学年を示すペールグリーンのジャージ。ミルクティーとレモンティーのあいだを太い指が逡巡している。僕はそのうしろに並んで待った。
lines.english: His pale-green tracksuit marked him as another first-year. One thick finger wavered between the milk tea and the lemon tea while I waited behind him.

lines.japanese: たっぷり悩んでいた彼もやがては決断し、落ちてきたミルクティーと釣り銭を回収して自販機から離れた。
lines.english: After giving the matter ample thought, he made his choice, collected the milk tea and his change, and stepped away.

lines.japanese: 代わって僕は一歩前へ進んだ。だけどお金を入れようとしたとき、耳のうしろでちゃりんとかすかな音が鳴った。
lines.english: I stepped forward to take his place. Just as I was about to put in my money, a faint chink sounded behind my ear.

lines.japanese: 振りむくと、ジャージの彼が小銭を財布に入れそこねて床にばら撒いていた。
lines.english: I turned. The boy in the tracksuit had missed his wallet and scattered his coins across the floor.

lines.japanese: 僕は持っていたパンとジュースを自動販売機の脇へ置き、腰を折りまげて一緒にそれを拾った。
lines.english: I set my bread and drinks beside the vending machine, bent down, and helped him gather them.

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Here.”

lines.japanese: 拾いあげた何枚かを手渡すと、彼はヘルメットみたいな頭をついっと前に突きだし、言葉もなく去っていった。
lines.english: I handed him the coins I had found. He bobbed his helmet-shaped head at me, then walked off without a word.

lines.japanese: 不機嫌な子供みたいなその歩き方をしばし見送ってから、自販機に向きなおった。
lines.english: I watched his sulky, childlike walk for a moment, then turned back to the machine.

lines.japanese: すると、あとから来た女子が僕に舌打ちの聞こえてきそうな一瞥を送りながら、硬貨投入口に手を伸ばしていた。
lines.english: A girl who had arrived behind me was already reaching for the coin slot. She gave me a look so sharp I could practically hear the click of her tongue.

lines.japanese: 「あ、すいません……」
lines.english: “Oh—sorry…”

lines.japanese: 僕は頭を前ではなく下へ傾けて、パンとジュースはそのままに、彼女の後ろへ並びなおした。
lines.english: I lowered my head instead of jutting it forward and took my place behind her, leaving the bread and drinks where they were.

lines.japanese: 彼女はお金を入れたあと、悠々と長考してから烏龍茶を選んだ。
lines.english: After inserting her money, she considered her options at regal leisure and chose the oolong tea.

lines.japanese: 女子が去ったあと、ふたたび自販機の前に立った。
lines.english: When she had gone, I stood before the machine once more.

lines.japanese: 押そうとしていた黒いボタンには、赤い文字が無愛想に浮かびあがっていた。
lines.english: Red letters glared without sympathy from the black button I had been about to press.

lines.japanese: 『売切』。
lines.english: SOLD OUT.

lines.japanese: 呆気に取られる暇もなく、声と体の大きな三年生たちがのしのしやってきて、僕の後ろに順番待ちの列を作った。
lines.english: Before I had time to absorb the blow, a group of large, loud third-years came thudding up and formed a line behind me.

lines.japanese: テメーラマジ殺スゾとか叫ぶような冗談を飛ばしあっている。せっかちな八つの目が、僕の背中に苛立っている気がした。僕は空白の思考で、とにかく烏龍茶のすぐ横のボタンを押した。
lines.english: They traded jokes that involved bellowing things like, “I'm seriously gonna kill you assholes!” I could feel all eight impatient eyes boring into my back. My mind went blank. I pressed the button next to the oolong tea.

lines.japanese: 体を自販機の横へ逃がしながら、取り出し口を開けて、落ちてきた黄緑色のパックを掴む。運だめしの結果は、うぐいす餡と相性の悪そうなプレーンの豆乳だった。
lines.english: I fled to the side of the machine, opened the hatch, and grabbed the pale-green carton that had fallen out. My blind choice had yielded plain soy milk, a poor companion for sweet green-pea paste.

lines.japanese: その場を三年生に譲った僕は、脇に置いておいた荷物を拾おうとした。
lines.english: Having surrendered the machine to the third-years, I bent to retrieve the things I had left beside it.

lines.japanese: 目の前を短いスカートとその下に伸びた太い脚がよぎる、と思ったら上履きのゴムがあっけなくブルガリを弾きとばしていった。
lines.english: A short skirt and the stout legs beneath it crossed my field of vision. An indoor shoe clipped one of the Bulgaris and sent it skittering away.

lines.japanese: 気付かなかったのか気付かなかった振りをしたのか、その女生徒は一顧だにせず、そのまますたすたと歩きさっていった。
lines.english: Whether she failed to notice or merely pretended not to, the girl never spared it a glance. She strode on without breaking pace.

lines.japanese: 飛んでいったブルガリを追って屈んだまま横切る僕を、通りかかった二年生のカップルが、水族館の爬虫類でも眺めるような目で見下ろしていた。
lines.english: Still crouching, I scuttled after the fugitive Bulgari. A passing couple of second-years looked down at me as though I were a reptile behind glass at the aquarium.

lines.japanese: 四角い紙パックを拾いあげながら、脈絡もなく僕は祈った。
lines.english: As I picked up the square carton, I found myself praying for no particular reason.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: 「おおー、さんきゅさんきゅ」
lines.english: “Hey, thanks. Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 教室の扉を開けると、森里君が小走りで駆けよってきて、荷台代わりの腕から三つの紙パックを引きとってくれた。
lines.english: When I opened the classroom door, Morisato trotted over and relieved my makeshift loading rack of its three cartons.

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Sure.”

lines.japanese: 僕は笑顔で応えた。
lines.english: I smiled at him.

lines.japanese: 「遅かったじゃん。昼休み終わっちゃうかと思ったよ」
lines.english: “Took you long enough. I thought lunch break was gonna end.”

lines.japanese: 彼は笑わずに、女の子みたいに細く刈りそろえられた山型の眉をひそめた。
lines.english: He didn't smile back. His eyebrows—trimmed into slender arches almost delicate enough for a girl's face—drew together.

lines.japanese: 「あ……ごめん、自分のパンとか買ってたから」
lines.english: “Oh… sorry. I was buying my own lunch too.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まあ、いいって。また頼むな」
lines.english: “Well, whatever. It's fine. I'll ask you again sometime.”

lines.japanese: 森里君は快く許してくれた。やっぱりいいひとだ。彼がそのまま背中を向けて歩きだしたので、僕はそのうしろに付いていった。
lines.english: Morisato forgave me readily. He really was a good person. When he turned his back and walked away, I followed.

lines.japanese: 教室の最後列にあった机ひとつを、ふたりの男子生徒が囲んでいた。彼らはぴたりとお喋りをやめ、森里君からの配給を受けとりながら、じっと僕の立ち姿を見詰めていた。
lines.english: Two boys were gathered around a desk in the last row. They fell silent as Morisato distributed the supplies, watching me where I stood.

lines.japanese: その視線を追うように、森里君が僕に振りかえった。
lines.english: Following their eyes, Morisato turned back to me.
“Mm… What?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 質問の意図が分からず、僕は曖昧に笑いながらうぐいすパンの袋を開けた。
lines.english: I didn’t understand the question. Smiling vaguely, I opened the wrapper on my sweet green-pea bun.

lines.japanese: 「……ああ、あれ、ここで食べんの」
lines.english: “…Oh. That. You're eating it here?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。おれ、昼ごはん今からなんだ」
lines.english: “Yes. I haven't had lunch yet.”

lines.japanese: 「あー……ああ、そうなん」
lines.english: “Oh… Right. Gotcha.”

lines.japanese: 森里君たちはひととき静かに顔を見合わせた。
lines.english: Morisato and his friends exchanged a quiet look.

lines.japanese: 「あー……じゃあ、まあ、座ればその辺……」
lines.english: “Well… sure. Grab a seat somewhere, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ありがと」
lines.english: “Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 森里君が指差した空の席に、僕は椅子を引いて腰を落とした。
lines.english: I pulled out the chair he had pointed to and sat down.

lines.japanese: 僕が座った席と、みんなが囲んでいた机とのあいだには、誰かがすんなり通れるぐらいの隙間があった。
lines.english: Between my seat and the desk they had gathered around was a gap wide enough for anyone to walk through.

lines.japanese: 黄緑色のブリック容器にストローを刺して一口吸いあげたとき、彼らがそろって僕を注視していることに気付いた。
lines.english: I pushed a straw into the pale-green carton and took a sip. That was when I realized all three of them were staring at me.

lines.japanese: なんらかの反応を示さないわけにはいかず、僕は慌てて口にするべき言葉を探した。
lines.english: I had to say something. Flustered, I searched for words.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ、７０円足りなかったよ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. You were seventy yen short.”
“Huh? Oh—”

lines.japanese: 森里君は首を曲げ、集まっていた机の持ち主である大柄な男子に言った。
lines.english: Morisato craned his neck toward the large boy whose desk they had commandeered.

lines.japanese: 「──だってさ」
lines.english: “—he says.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、俺に言うなよ。サトシだろ」
lines.english: “Why're you telling me? That was Satoshi.”

lines.japanese: 「んーでだよ、オメーだって半分しか出してねーべ」
lines.english: “The hell it was. You only put in half your share too.”

lines.japanese: 僕はうぐいすパンをかじりながら、彼らの張りのない論争を黙って聞いていた。喉の奥に豆乳がまとわりついて、なんだかすっきりしなかった。
lines.english: I ate my sweet green-pea bun and listened in silence to their listless dispute. Soy milk clung to the back of my throat, leaving me vaguely dissatisfied.

lines.japanese: 「てかさあ、オメそーゆートコせこいから女に捨てられるンだって」
lines.english: “See, this cheap shit is exactly why girls dump you.”

lines.japanese: 「だァら！　ちげェつってんじゃん。ありゃこっちから切ったんだっつーの」
lines.english: “For the last time, she didn't dump me. I dumped her.”

lines.japanese: 「までも、そら正解だろ。寝てる隙に男のケータイ見るような女はやべーって実際」
lines.english: “Either way, good call. A girl who checks your phone while you're asleep is bad news.”

lines.japanese: 「や、それはべつにお互い様だからいンだけどー」
lines.english: “Nah, that part was fine. We both did it.”

lines.japanese: 「おめーも見てんのかよ！」
lines.english: “You checked hers too?”

lines.japanese: 「あははは」
lines.english: “Ahahaha.”

lines.japanese: 僕がみんなといっしょに笑ったら、その大柄な彼が、建築現場の回頭する重機みたいにのっそりこちらを向いた。
lines.english: I laughed along with the others. The big boy slowly swung around to face me, like a piece of heavy machinery turning on a construction site.
“Ha… ha…”

lines.japanese: 僕は下を向いてサンドウィッチの封を切った。青臭さが鼻をつく。やっぱりキュウリは嫌いだ。
lines.english: I looked down and tore open the wrapper on my sandwich. The raw green smell struck my nose. I really did hate cucumber.

lines.japanese: 「いやいやイヤイヤ、だってな？」
lines.english: “No, no, no, listen, okay?”

lines.japanese: 彼は視点を戻して大きな声で続ける。
lines.english: He swung his gaze back around and went on at full volume.

lines.japanese: 「マジおかしンだって、あの女！　メールが１日２０オーバーとかってヤバくね？　ヤベえだろ？」
lines.english: “I’m telling you, this chick is seriously nuts! More than twenty texts a day—isn’t that bad? That’s bad, right?”

lines.japanese: 「そーかぁ？　夜中とか盛りあがってテンション上がりまくりゃ、何気にそんぐれー行くべ」
lines.english: “Is it? You get talking late at night, things heat up, you’re both all wired—I could see it hitting twenty easy.”

lines.japanese: 「違くて、ラリーしてねーのに一方的にガァー送ってくんだよ。誰と会ってんだとか今すぐ会いたいとか。ネタじゃなくてよ？　すんげ、ガチなやつよ？」
lines.english: “That’s not what I mean. There is no back-and-forth. She just machine-guns them at me. Who’re you with, I wanna see you right now, all that. And this isn’t some bit, okay? She’s dead serious.”

lines.japanese: 「うーわ、そりゃたしかに引くな。怖えーよソレ、どこのサスペンス劇場だよ」
lines.english: “Whoa. Okay, that is creepy. What is this, some kind of TV thriller?”

lines.japanese: 「あァその女、そりゃ病んでんな。つうかアレだ、イゾンショーだ」
lines.english: “Yeah, that girl’s got issues. Whaddaya call it—dependency disorder.”

lines.japanese: 「てかさ、その女、なんでこんなデブにそこまでハマれんの。そっからすでにありえなくね？」
lines.english: “But seriously, what does she see in a fatass like you? That part already makes no sense.”

lines.japanese: 「っせーな、ひがんでんじゃねーよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Don’t get bitter just ’cause you’re jealous.”

lines.japanese: 彼は肘を使って友人を小突いた。みんなが笑う。僕は（今度は）声を出さない程度に頬を緩めた。
lines.english: He dug an elbow into his friend. Everyone laughed. This time, I let myself smile—though not enough to make a sound.

lines.japanese: 「あ、分かった分かった。そいつＢ専だろ。ブサ専ブサ専」
lines.english: “Oh, I got it, I got it. She’s got an ugly-guy fetish. That’s totally it.”

lines.japanese: 「も、ええっつの。しつけーよ、んな引っぱる話じゃねンだよ」
lines.english: “All right, enough. Quit milking it. It wasn’t even that big a story.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ話変えっけどォ、あんさァ、タデ食う虫も好き好きのタデって何なん？」
lines.english: “Okay, change of subject—hey, you know that saying, ‘Some bugs even like water pepper’? What the hell is water pepper?”

lines.japanese: 「テメそれ、話変わってねーじゃねえか！」
lines.english: “You asshole, that’s the same damn subject!”

lines.japanese: 「くっくっく」
lines.english: “Heh heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、森里君」
lines.english: “Um, Morisato?”

lines.japanese: 僕は斜めに手を掲げた。彼の求める答えを、たまたまネット上で読んだことがあって知っていた。
lines.english: I raised one hand at an angle. By sheer chance, I had once read the answer he wanted online.

lines.japanese: 「あの、それ、蓼っていう水辺とかに生えてる植物でね、たしか苦くて辛くて独特の匂いがあるって──」
lines.english: “It's a plant called water pepper. It grows near the water, and I think it's bitter and hot and has a really distinctive smell—”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ああ、そーなんだ……」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh. That right…”

lines.japanese: 「うん。でも蓼にはいろんな種類があって、全部が辛いとは限らないんだけど……あ、そういえば蕎麦とか藍も蓼科の一種なんだよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. But there are lots of different kinds, and they aren’t all hot… Oh, and buckwheat and indigo are in the same family.”

lines.japanese: 「……へぇー」
lines.english: “…Wow.”

lines.japanese: 「……すっげ、超ウケるな。トリビアってやつか、いまどき」
lines.english: “…Whoa. That’s hilarious. Trivia, huh? Who even does that anymore?”

lines.japanese: 「つうかアレだ、マジレスだ」
lines.english: “Nah, man. He gave you a serious answer.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。すげーな羽田クン。物知り羽田じゃん」
lines.english: “Huh. Would you look at that. Encyclopedia Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことないけど……はは」
lines.english: “I—I’m really not… Ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 「で？　物知り羽田は彼女とかいんの？」
lines.english: “So? Does Encyclopedia Haneda have a girlfriend?”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: いきなりそんなことを聞かれて、僕はきょとんとしてしまった。
lines.english: The question came so suddenly that I could only stare.

lines.japanese: 「いや、『え』じゃなくて。いま俺ら、そーゆー話してたんだけど」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘what’ me. That’s what we’ve been talking about this whole time.”

lines.japanese: 「おめ、聞くなよ。さりげにイジメじゃん、それ」
lines.english: “Dude, don’t ask him that. That’s low-key bullying.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでよ、決めつける方がひでーべ？　なあ羽田クン、その辺どうなのよ」
lines.english: “How? Deciding he doesn’t without asking would be way meaner. So, Haneda—what’s the story?”

lines.japanese: どうもこうもない。僕はそれまで彼女とか恋愛とかについてなんか、縁がないどころか考えたことすらなかったんだ。
lines.english: There was no story. Up to then, girlfriends and romance had been more than merely beyond my reach. I had never even thought about them.

lines.japanese: 「え、いないよ、そんなの」
lines.english: “No. I don’t have anyone like that.”

lines.japanese: 「え・え・え、ええ～っ！　マママ、マぁぁジでぇぇ～！？」
lines.english: “W-w-w-whaaat? You’re s-s-seriously serious?!”

lines.japanese: 「くせえリアクションすんなよ、俺の羽田クンがかあいそーだろ」
lines.english: “Cut the corny reaction. You’re making my poor Haneda feel bad.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、だってチョー意外だよ、羽田クンめっさモテそーなのに」
lines.english: “No, but seriously, that’s a huge surprise. Haneda, you look like you’d be crazy popular.”

lines.japanese: 「まさか、そんな、あはは」
lines.english: “No, no, not at all. Ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 「うっはー、こいつ謙遜してるよ。やーっべ、羽田チョー殊勝じゃん」
lines.english: “Oh, wow, listen to him play it humble. Damn, Haneda. Aren't you modest.”

lines.japanese: 「でもさあ、好きなやつぐらいいんだろ？」
lines.english: “Come on, though. There’s gotta be somebody you like.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いないよ！」
lines.english: “Th-there isn’t!”

lines.japanese: 僕はぶんぶん手を振りながら正直に答えた。すると、あの大きな体の彼が黄ばんだ歯を見せて笑った。
lines.english: I waved both hands frantically and answered in all honesty. The large boy flashed a grin full of yellowed teeth.

lines.japanese: 「ああ？　うそだろォ、その反応は怪しくねーかあオイ」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah? Bullshit. That reaction’s looking awfully suspicious, man.”

lines.japanese: 「怪しいって、めちゃめちゃ怪しいって。なー、教えてよ羽田クン、誰にも言わねーからさあ」
lines.english: “Suspicious? It’s screaming guilty. C’mon, Haneda, tell us. We won’t tell anybody.”

lines.japanese: 「え、でも、ごめん……ほんとにいないし……」
lines.english: “I’m sorry, but… there really isn’t anyone…”

lines.japanese: みんなが楽しそうに聞いてくるのは嬉しかったけど、残念ながらその頃の僕は、本当に彼らの期待に添えるような回答を持ちあわせていなかったんだ。
lines.english: I was glad they seemed so eager to hear my answer. Unfortunately, back then I truly had none that could live up to their expectations.

lines.japanese: 「オイオイ待てって羽田、逆にやべーだろソレは。不健全だって。男として終わってるって」
lines.english: “Whoa, hold on, Haneda. That’s bad in a whole different way. It’s unhealthy. You’re finished as a man.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかな」
lines.english: “You think?”

lines.japanese: 「終わってる終わってる。×んこ壊疽してんじゃねーの。だったら切んねーと全身腐るぜ？」
lines.english: “Finished. Totally finished. Your d×ck's probably gone gangrenous. Better cut it off before your whole body rots.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。やべーじゃん羽田。モロッコ羽田じゃん」
lines.english: “For real? That’s bad, Haneda. You’re gonna be Morocco Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「なあ、ちょっとおまえらさ、俺らで羽田に彼女できるよう協力してやんね？」
lines.english: “Hey, guys—why don’t we help Haneda get himself a girlfriend?”

lines.japanese: 「おほっ？　いいねその企画、面白そうじゃん」
lines.english: “Oho? Now there’s a plan. Sounds fun.”

lines.japanese: 「ばかおまえ、面白いとかじゃねンだよ。羽田クンの命かかってんだよ。うちら羽田クンの友達だかんな、友達の命は救わねーと。で、で、具体的にどーすんよ？」
lines.english: “Idiot, this isn’t about fun. Haneda’s life is on the line. We’re his friends, and friends save each other’s lives. So? So? What do we actually do?”

lines.japanese: そう言ってみんながにこにこしながら僕の周りに集まってきた。みんな楽しそうに笑ってる。
lines.english: They gathered around me as they spoke, all smiles. Every one of them looked delighted.

lines.japanese: 輪の中心。入学以来、初めての快挙だ。
lines.english: The center of the circle. My first great triumph since entering school.

lines.japanese: 「でもいいよ、そんな。おれ、そういうの向いてないし、今のとこ興味もないから」
lines.english: “No, really, I’m fine. I’m not cut out for that kind of thing, and right now I’m not interested.”

lines.japanese: 「だァらオメ、そゆこと言ってっとカラダ腐んだって」
lines.english: “That’s what I’m telling you—keep talking like that and your body’s gonna rot.”

lines.japanese: 森里君がいつものように僕のうしろから腕を絡めてきた。甘い香水の匂い。
lines.english: As he always did, Morisato looped an arm around me from behind. His perfume smelled sweet.

lines.japanese: 「とりあえずさー、標的決めようぜ、標的ー。相手いねーことにはラヴも始まんねーじゃん」
lines.english: “First things first, let’s pick a target. A target. You can’t start a romance without somebody to romance.”

lines.japanese: 森里君はペットショップを訪れたお客さんみたいに、教室に点在する白いセーラー服の姿をぐるりと見渡していた。
lines.english: Like a customer browsing a pet shop, Morisato swept his gaze over the white sailor uniforms scattered around the classroom.

lines.japanese: 「だ、だからいいってば。それに、そういうのって、そんな適当に決めることでもないと思うし」
lines.english: “I said I’m fine. Besides, I don’t think you can just pick someone at random like that.”

lines.japanese: 「青いよォ羽田クン～。んな、レンアイなんて、きっかけと思い込みだって。好きンなろうと思やー簡単になれるもんよ？」
lines.english: “You're so green, Haneda. Love's nothing but an opening and a little self-delusion. Decide you're going to fall for someone and it's easy enough, see?”

lines.japanese: 彼は大人びた口調でラブソングの歌詞みたいなことを言った。
lines.english: He said it with the worldly assurance of a line from a love song.

lines.japanese: 「そこら辺のカップルつかまえて、相手のどこが好きか聞いてみ。どうせその答えの大半は後付けだぜ？」
lines.english: “Grab any couple around here and ask what they like about each other. Most of the answer’ll be something they came up with afterward anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「まずは一個の、適当なとっかかりなんだよ。顔がいいとか胸がでかいとか金持ってるとか。すべてのラヴはその適当な一個から始まんの」
lines.english: “All you need at first is one random little hook. A pretty face, a great rack, a fat bank account. Every romance starts with one random thing like that.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょ、なんで和馬あんなラブ仙人気取りなん？」
lines.english: “Wait, why’s Kazuma acting like some enlightened love guru?”

lines.japanese: 「なー。あいつ、いまどきラブコメみたいな純愛してるくせになー」
lines.english: “Right? When he's the one having a pure romance straight out of a rom-com.”

lines.japanese: 「ほっとけよ！　いーんだよ俺の話は！」
lines.english: “Leave me alone! We’re not talking about me!”

lines.japanese: 「羽田ホラ、オメーの話だよ。おー、おまえ好みのタイプとかあんの？」
lines.english: “Haneda, hey. We’re talking about you. So—what kind of girl do you like?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　さあ、べつに──」
lines.english: “What? I don’t know. No particular type—”

lines.japanese: 「そーりゃおまえ、羽田みたいのはアレだろ。童顔でこう、おとなしーカンジのさぁ。なんつーの、ほら、オタ受けしそうな？」
lines.english: “C'mon, with a guy like Haneda it's obvious. Baby-faced, quiet—you know the type. The kind nerds go for.”

lines.japanese: 「てーと樺島さんか。漫研の」
lines.english: “So, Kabashima? From the manga club?”

lines.japanese: 「いやオタじゃねーよ。オタ受けしそうな、つってんだよ」
lines.english: “No, I don’t mean a nerd. I mean the kind of girl nerds go for.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ロリ系？」
lines.english: “Oh. The loli type?”
“Under thirteen?”

lines.japanese: 「行きすぎ行きすぎ。こん中、該当者いねーじゃん」
lines.english: “Too far, too far. Nobody here qualifies.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ何なんだよオタ受けって。んん？　校門の陰で健気に先輩の帰りを待っちゃう系か？」
lines.english: “Then what does ‘the kind nerds go for’ even mean? Hmm? The kind who waits sweetly behind the school gates for her upperclassman to come home?”

lines.japanese: 「おお、萌えーってやつだ。髪は黒くてパンツは白って感じの。つうかアレだ、セージュン系だ」
lines.english: “Yeah, that’s the sweet-and-innocent type. Black hair, white panties, the whole package.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、それそれ。清純系」
lines.english: “That’s it. Pure and innocent.”

lines.japanese: 「つーと、うちのクラスで言ったら誰だ……えーと、あいつ、ヤマシナとか？」
lines.english: “So who’s that in our class… Uh, what about, y’know, Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「おー、山科京。マニアックなとこ突いてきたねェ」
lines.english: “Oh, Miyako Yamashina. That’s a deep cut.”

lines.japanese: 「うっそ、山科ぁ？　アレおとなしそうっつーか、ジャンル的には『暗そう』の部類じゃね？」
lines.english: “Seriously? Yamashina? She’s less the quiet type and more the ‘looks depressed’ type, isn’t she?”

lines.japanese: 「そーそー、だから羽田みたいのと合いそうじゃん」
lines.english: “Exactly. That’s why she sounds like a good match for somebody like Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「あるある。つーか、ぶっちゃけ俺的にも、山科全然アリなんですけど。なんかほら、惚れた男にだけはスッゲー尽くしそうな感じすんじゃん」
lines.english: “Yeah, I see it. Honestly, I’d be totally down for Yamashina myself. She’s got that vibe like once she falls for a guy, she’d do absolutely anything for him.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、たしかに口ですんのとかは上手そうな顔だよなアレ」
lines.english: “Yeah, she does kinda look like she’d be good with her mouth.”

lines.japanese: 「かかか、同級生捕まえてフェラ美人って、おまえソレどんだけセクハラだよ」
lines.english: “Ka-ka-ka! Calling your own classmate a blowjob beauty? That is some next-level sexual harassment.”

lines.japanese: 「いやでもさ、なんつーかマジな話、黙って三歩あとを付いてきそうな感じはするよな」
lines.english: “No, but seriously. She does seem like the type who’d follow her man three paces behind without a word.”

lines.japanese: 「おー、いい表現ねソレ、黙って三歩あとを？　はぁ、やっぱ男ってなんだかんだ言っても、最後はみんなそういう従順系に帰結すんのかねえ」
lines.english: “Ooh, nice phrase. Three paces behind, without a word? Man, maybe no matter what guys say, in the end we all come home to the sweet, obedient type.”

lines.japanese: 「や、でも山科ムリだぜ。あいつ、オトコいんらしーもん。たしか、大学生の元家庭教師とかって」
lines.english: “Yeah, but Yamashina’s out. I hear she’s already got a guy. Some college student who used to tutor her, I think.”

lines.japanese: 「ムぁジでぇ！？　かァー、ヘコむなそれ。せっかく俺が入学式の日から目ぇ付けてたのによー」
lines.english: “Are you serious?! Damn, that hurts. And here I’ve had my eye on her since the entrance ceremony.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、付けるだけなら俺だって軽く３０人は付けてっけどさあ」
lines.english: “If having your eye on them counts, I’ve got at least thirty on my list.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ちょ、どうするよ羽田。山科、オトコいるってよ」
lines.english: “Uh-oh. What now, Haneda? Yamashina’s got a man.”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうするって言われても、べつにどうも……」
lines.english: “What do you mean, what now? I don’t really…”

lines.japanese: そもそも僕はまだその頃、クラス全員の顔と名前を覚えてなくて、山科さんって言われても誰のことかすら分かっていなかった。
lines.english: At the time, I still had not learned all my classmates’ faces and names. When they said ‘Yamashina,’ I did not even know whom they meant.

lines.japanese: 「オイオイどーすんだよ羽田、一発目からいきなり失恋じゃん。おまえそんな、パン食ってる場合じゃねーって」
lines.english: “Whoa, what’re you gonna do, Haneda? First try out and you’re already heartbroken. This is no time to sit there eating bread.”

lines.japanese: 「まァまァそんな落ちこむなって羽田。次がある次が。な、他にどんなん好きなの」
lines.english: “There, there, don’t take it so hard, Haneda. There’ll be another one. So, what else are you into?”

lines.japanese: 「さ、さぁ……とくには……」
lines.english: “I—I don’t know… Nothing in particular…”

lines.japanese: 「とかゆーやつに限って、理想だきゃーバリ高だったりすんだよなー。見た目ばっか贅沢言ったりさー。ぜってーそうだよ」
lines.english: “Guys who say that always turn out to have sky-high standards. All picky about looks and everything. Bet you anything that’s it.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。すげーじゃん羽田。面食い羽田じゃん」
lines.english: “For real? Damn, Haneda. So you're a face guy. Face-First Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「まー、童貞って夢見がちな季節だからねー」
lines.english: “Well, virginity is the season of dreams.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、それは責めちゃいけない。それは許してあげよう。男の子ならＤＴはみんな通ってきた道だ」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, you can't hold that against him. We can let him have that. Every boy passes through the V-card stage.”

lines.japanese: 「おーし、じゃあ、やっぱ高め狙ってくかァ。夢や理想は高い方がいいって、園長センセーも朝礼で言ってた言ってた」
lines.english: “All right, then let’s aim high. Higher is better when it comes to hopes and dreams. The principal said so at morning assembly. Definitely said so.”

lines.japanese: 「おー、言ってた言ってた」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah. Definitely did.”

lines.japanese: 「言ってた言ってたじゃねーよ。おめーら、朝礼出たことねーだろ」
lines.english: “Quit saying ‘definitely did.’ Neither of you has ever gone to morning assembly.”

lines.japanese: 森里君たちは僕の頭の上で、僕を含めずに、僕のための会議を始めた。
lines.english: Over my head, Morisato and the others began holding a meeting about me, for my sake, without me.

lines.japanese: 僕は背中で森里君の体重を支えながら、もそもそと食事を進めた。昼休みが終わるまでには、まだあと１０分も残されていた。
lines.english: With my back bearing Morisato’s weight, I quietly worked my way through my lunch. There were still ten whole minutes until the end of the break.

lines.japanese: 「ハイそれでは、理想も高く！　ででんっ、渡来明日香っ！」
lines.english: “Okay, then—standards high! Drumroll, please: Asuka Watarai!”

lines.japanese: 「おっほー！　トップ目来たァー！」
lines.english: “Oho! Straight for number one!”

lines.japanese: みんなの目が忍びがちに一点へ向かった。窓辺に寄りあつまっているセーラー服の数人。
lines.english: Every eye stole toward a single point: a cluster of girls in sailor uniforms gathered by the windows.

lines.japanese: 中にひとり、場違いなほど際立った存在感を放つ女子がいた。鈍い僕でさえ、話題の焦点が彼女であることはすぐに理解できた。
lines.english: One girl among them possessed a presence so vivid it seemed out of place. Even I, slow as I was, understood at once that she was the object of discussion.

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿おまえ、明日香さまはトップとかそーゆー次元じゃねーって。やべーよアレ、笑った顔とか正直アイドル入ってんじゃん。俺、あいつと目ェ合ったらフツーに緊張すんもん」
lines.english: “Idiot, Lady Asuka is beyond rankings. She’s unreal. When she smiles, she’s honestly idol-tier. If our eyes meet, I get nervous for real.”

lines.japanese: 「いや緊張っつーか、むしろこう、朝のだりぃときとか渡来がフッて横通ると、ッシャァァーって気になるよな」
lines.english: “Nervous? More like, when you’re dead on your feet in the morning and Watarai glides past, suddenly you’re all, hell yeah!”

lines.japanese: 「や、だから、あいつ出てんだってなんか。ぶわーってこう、新陳代謝を活発にする成分とか」
lines.english: “That’s what I’m saying. She gives something off. Some kind of compound that comes whooshing out and fires up your metabolism.”

lines.japanese: 「マジでか。もはや歩くアロマテラピーだな。つうかアレだ、マイナスイオンだ」
lines.english: “Seriously? She’s walking aromatherapy. Wait, I got it—negative ions.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、森里君。それなんだけど、実はマイナスイオンが非科学的だっていう説もあってね」
lines.english: “Actually, Morisato, there's a theory that negative ions are unscientific, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「あー悪り、関係ないやつはちょっと黙ってて。でよー、正直どーなのよ渡来は」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. If this doesn’t concern you, keep quiet for a sec. So, seriously, what do you guys think of Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、どーもこーもねえって。分析不可だよ。あんなんもう、人種ちげンだよ俺らとは」
lines.english: “There’s nothing to think. She defies analysis. She’s like a whole different species from us.”

lines.japanese: 「だよなー。もうある意味、やりてーって気にすらならねえもんな。まあ、そんなわけで？　俺らじゃとても敵わないから？」
lines.english: “Right? In a way, she’s so far beyond us you don’t even get horny. So, since none of us could possibly compete…”

lines.japanese: 「からっ？」
lines.english: “Sooo?”

lines.japanese: 不意にみんなが顔を寄せてきた。どの表情も、吹きだしそうな笑いを堪えてるみたいだった。
lines.english: All at once, their faces crowded close. Every one of them looked ready to burst out laughing.

lines.japanese: 「おまえに譲るよ、羽田」
lines.english: “She’s all yours, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 僕は呑気にサンドイッチにかぶりついているところだった。
lines.english: I happened to be taking an unconcerned bite of my sandwich.
“…What?”

lines.japanese: 「え、じゃねーって。ほら、いま明日香さま呼んできてやっから。ガッツン行っとけー？」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘what’ us. We’ll go get Lady Asuka right now, so shoot your shot, okay?”
“What? What?”

lines.japanese: 大柄な彼は見かけのわりに行動が早かった。
lines.english: For someone so large, he moved surprisingly fast.

lines.japanese: 窓辺に寄りあつまっていたセーラー服の一団に近付いていったかと思うや、へらへら笑ったりぺこぺこ頭を下げたりして──
lines.english: He made straight for the knot of sailor uniforms beside the windows, grinning foolishly and bowing over and over—

lines.japanese: 「羽田ぁ、連れてきたぞー」
lines.english: “Haneda! Brought her over!”

lines.japanese: ──僕が口の中のパンと野菜を呑みこんでるあいだにも戻ってきた。
lines.english: —and returned before I had even swallowed the bread and vegetables in my mouth.

lines.japanese: あの髪の長い女子を従えて。
lines.english: The girl with the long hair followed behind him.

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 知らない親戚にでも向けるような硬い笑顔で、彼女は座っている僕を正面から見下ろしていた。
lines.english: Wearing the stiff smile one might offer an unfamiliar relative, she stood directly before me and looked down.
“What?”

lines.japanese: 僕はそのとき、初めて彼女の顔を視界の正面に収めた。
lines.english: For the first time, her face occupied the center of my vision.

lines.japanese: てのひらで覆えそうなほど小さいキャンバスに、色の薄い唇と、くっきりした二重まぶたの瞳が絶妙に配置されていた。白状すると、ひと目見て可愛いと思った。
lines.english: On a canvas small enough to hide behind one palm, pale lips and eyes beneath sharply defined double lids had been set in exquisite balance. I confess: at first sight, I thought she was pretty.

lines.japanese: でも、ふだん黒板か教科書か窓の外を見ていることがほとんどの僕は、そのときまだ渡来明日香という彼女の名前すら知らなかった。
lines.english: But I spent most of my time looking at the blackboard, my textbooks, or the world beyond the window. At that point, I did not yet know even her name: Asuka Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「なにって……え、なに？」
lines.english: “What do you mean…? Um, what?”

lines.japanese: どぎまぎしながら質問をそのまま返すと、渡来さんは言葉に詰まって森里君たちに視線を滑らせた。
lines.english: Flustered, I merely returned her question. Watarai faltered, then slid her gaze toward Morisato and the others.

lines.japanese: 「羽田ぁ、この期に及んで照れンなってー」
lines.english: “C’mon, Haneda. Little late to get shy on us now.”

lines.japanese: 森里君が僕の体に寄りかかったまま、首を絞めて揺すぶる。
lines.english: Still leaning his weight against me, Morisato locked an arm around my neck and shook me.

lines.japanese: 「ま、しょーがねえか。そんだけ本気っつーことなんだよな？」
lines.english: “Well, can’t blame you, I guess. Just shows how serious you are, right?”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。すげーじゃん羽田。ロマンス羽田じゃん」
lines.english: “Damn, Haneda. Look at you. Haneda the Romantic.”

lines.japanese: 「そんじゃあ、羽田クンに代わって俺らが言ってやろっかあ」
lines.english: “Why don’t we tell her for Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「え、なに……森里君？」
lines.english: “Tell her what…? Morisato?”

lines.japanese: 彼らの笑顔に不穏な気配を感じて僕は振りむこうとした。
lines.english: Their smiles carried a hint of menace. I tried to turn around.

lines.japanese: 「こいつがね、渡来さん」
lines.english: “See, Watarai…”

lines.japanese: しかし僕の頭は、うしろからがっちりと抑えられていた。
lines.english: But my head was pinned firmly in place from behind.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんのこと好きなんだってぇー」
lines.english: “…this guy says he’s in love with you.”

lines.japanese: 「ちがっ……」
lines.english: “That’s not—”

lines.japanese: 僕は悲鳴みたいな声をあげて、机を挟んで立つ渡来さんの表情を見上げた。
lines.english: My voice rose almost to a scream as I looked up at Watarai across the desk, searching her face.

lines.japanese: 彼女は澄んだ瞳を丸く膨らませ、ささやかに開けた小さな唇を困惑の形に留めていた。
lines.english: Her clear eyes had gone round. Her small lips hung slightly parted, caught in a shape of bewilderment.

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　違うよ？　おれ、ぜんぜん、そんなこと言ってないからね？」
lines.english: “What? No, that isn’t true. I never said anything like that, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「はーねーだー、照れンなってぇ！」
lines.english: “Ha-ne-da! Don’t be shyyy!”

lines.japanese: 森里君はうしろから身を乗りだして、たぶん赤くなりかけている僕の顔のすぐ横に自分の顔を並べた。
lines.english: Morisato leaned out from behind me and brought his face alongside mine, which was probably beginning to redden.

lines.japanese: そして視線を上げてもう一言。
lines.english: Then he looked up and added one more thing.

lines.japanese: 「ちゅーか、ぶっちゃけ付きあってほしいんだって」
lines.english: “Matter of fact, he wants you to go out with him.”

lines.japanese: 「や、やめてよ」
lines.english: “S-stop it.”

lines.japanese: 僕は背中に貼りついていた悪意を引きはがし、振りかえりながら立ちあがった。
lines.english: I tore the malice from my back and rose, turning on him.

lines.japanese: 恥ずかしさとか悔しさとか、そんなのじゃない。彼の言動の意図が分からず、その理解できないという苛立ちに眩暈がしそうだった。
lines.english: It was not embarrassment, nor was it wounded pride. I could not understand what he meant by any of this, and the frustration of not understanding made me dizzy.

lines.japanese: 「なんなのそれ……え、どういうことだよ……」
lines.english: “What is this…? What are you doing…?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: すがるように森里君の肩を掴むと、彼は任侠映画に出てくる三下みたいなしかめ面で僕を見詰めかえした。
lines.english: I clutched Morisato’s shoulder as if begging him for help. He stared back with the scowl of a two-bit thug from a yakuza movie.
“Hanedaaa…”

lines.japanese: 「オメ～はよォ～、エエ～？　なあ。なあコラ。ああッ！？　ドサクサに紛れて何でけェクチきいてん──」
lines.english: “You little—huh? Hey. Hey, punk! What the fuck?! Don’t think you can get away with mouthing off just ’cause everyone’s distracted—”

lines.japanese: 彼が攻撃性の意思をもってその手を伸ばしてきたので──
lines.english: He reached for me, openly intending violence—
“Hk!”

lines.japanese: 僕は咄嗟にそれを捕まえて──
lines.english: I caught his hand on instinct—

lines.japanese: 「つあっ！」
lines.english: “Gah!”

lines.japanese: ──そのまま半円を描くようにひねった。森里君の動きは、手負いのグリズリーよりもはるかに遅かった。
lines.english: —and twisted it through a half circle. Morisato moved far more slowly than a wounded grizzly.

lines.japanese: 「なんなんだよ森里君、意味わかんないよ」
lines.english: “What is wrong with you, Morisato? None of this makes any sense.”

lines.japanese: 「く……て、てめえっ！」
lines.english: “Gh… Y-you bastard!”

lines.japanese: 首筋を這いのぼってくる寒気をこらえて僕は懇願した。
lines.english: I held back the chill crawling up my neck and pleaded with him.

lines.japanese: 「やめてよ、なんでそんな嘘つくんだよ」
lines.english: “Stop it. Why would you lie like that?”

lines.japanese: 「い、痛てっ！　離せバカ……！」
lines.english: “Ow! Let go, you idiot…!”

lines.japanese: 逃れようともがく手首。
lines.english: His wrist struggled to escape.

lines.japanese: 僕の握力に熱がこもる。
lines.english: Heat gathered in my grip.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: 「いいよ」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: そのとき、思いもかけない言葉がその場に降って湧いた。
lines.english: Then, out of nowhere, came words I never expected.

lines.japanese: 瞬間、僕は森里君に突きはなされ、椅子の上にどさりと押しもどされた。
lines.english: In the next instant, Morisato shoved me away. I dropped heavily back into my chair.

lines.japanese: 間の悪い沈黙の中、彼は僕を見詰め、僕は彼女を見上げていた。
lines.english: An awkward silence fell. He stared at me; I stared up at her.
“…Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「え……いいって、なにが……？」
lines.english: “What… What’s all right?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、いまの話」
lines.english: “What you just said.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは耳のうしろへ長い髪を流した。僕も森里君もみんな、呼吸の仕方を忘れたみたいにぽかんと口を開けていた。
lines.english: Watarai swept her long hair behind one ear. Morisato, the others, and I were all openmouthed, as though we had forgotten how to breathe.

lines.japanese: 「い、いまの話って……」
lines.english: “What we just said…?”

lines.japanese: 「まさか……」
lines.english: “You don’t mean…”

lines.japanese: <10>\「羽田と付きあうって話！？」
lines.english: “You mean going out with Haneda?!”

lines.japanese: 詰めよる男子たちの勢いに、渡来さんはたじろぎもせずににっこり微笑んだ。
lines.english: The boys pressed in on her. Watarai did not flinch; she simply smiled.

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Mm-hm.”

lines.japanese: 「は、ははっ……」
lines.english: “Ha… ha ha…”

lines.japanese: 釣りこまれたようにみんなも笑う。
lines.english: As if drawn in by it, everyone else laughed too.

lines.japanese: 「あ、はは……いや、びびったー……渡来さん真顔で言うんだもん、オモシロ過ぎ」
lines.english: “Ah-ha-ha… Wow, you scared me. You said it with such a straight face, Watarai. That was too good.”

lines.japanese: 「や、冗談じゃなくて。ほんとにほんとに」
lines.english: “No, it wasn't a joke. I really, really mean it.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: それがＯＦＦスイッチになって、僕らは硬直した。
lines.english: Those words flipped the switch to OFF. We froze.
“Seriously?!”

lines.japanese: 沈黙を打ちやぶったのは同級生たちの驚愕だった。
lines.english: My classmates’ astonishment shattered the silence.

lines.japanese: 僕こそ叫びたい気分だった。
lines.english: I was the one who wanted to scream.

lines.japanese: そんな出来すぎた話があるわけないと分かっていながらも、その瞬間の僕は、冗談の範疇を越えた甘い戸惑いを胸の奥に感じてしまったんだ。
lines.english: I knew there could be no such storybook turn of events. Even so, in that moment, deep in my chest, I felt a sweet bewilderment that had gone beyond the bounds of any joke.
